title: gateway-identity.v1 — the signed identity the gateway forwards to the services behind it
description: The gateway resolves a bearer through identity's /internal/validate and forwards the request with X-Vexa-Identity: "v1." + base64url(claims JSON) + "." + base64url(Ed25519 signature, by the gateway's private key, over "v1." + base64url(claims JSON)). "v1" fixes the scheme; nothing is negotiated. agent-api, meeting-api and the credential broker hold only the gateway's public key, so they verify and cannot sign: the signature, then the issue time and the expiry within a bounded clock skew. agent-api and meeting-api rebuild every x-user-* header from these claims and refuse with 401 a request that asserts an x-user-* header without a valid signature and without the internal tier's X-Internal-Secret. The credential broker refuses an agent-role call whose forwarded signature is missing, invalid or names a subject other than the assertion's actor.

sub.description: the user id identity resolved; becomes x-user-id

email.description: the verified email identity holds; becomes x-user-email

exp.description: expires at, unix seconds; a verifier refuses exp - iat > 300

Delegation.description: Present when the bearer was a worker's delegation token (vxd_). The ceiling the dispatch granted: a service refuses a person-in-the-loop verb when regime is not human.

workspaces.description: "*" (everything already the subject's) or the isolation set; becomes x-user-delegation-workspaces

target.description: the chat's target workspace, a default and never a grant; becomes x-user-delegation-target

ReentryHeader.description: MCP re-entry. A worker's delegation token (delegation.v1) is admitted by the gateway on /mcp only. The MCP's tools act by calling back into the gateway with the same bearer, so the MCP service (the carrier) holds the X-Vexa-Identity the gateway signed onto the /mcp request it is serving and sends it back, only on its calls to the gateway, in this header. The gateway (the only verifier) checks it with its own key's public half (signature, iat/exp within the skew and the 300 s lifetime) and admits the call only when the signed claims name the same sub as the bearer resolves to now AND carry a delegation equal to the bearer's (Reentry). The header is in the x-vexa-internal- family, which the gateway never forwards from a client to a service behind it. Header names are case-insensitive.

Reentry.description: A re-entry match vector, after the signature and lifetime checks have passed. `validation` is identity's /internal/validate answer for the bearer on the re-entering call (identity.v1 ValidateResponse); `signed` is the claims of the X-Vexa-Internal-Mcp-Identity token. `admitted` must equal: validation carries a delegation, AND signed.sub == str(validation.user_id), AND signed.delegation equals the delegation the gateway would sign for validation (regime, workspaces, target).

Vector.description: A signing test vector: any implementation signing these claims at `now` with the RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 1 key must produce `token` (Ed25519 signatures are deterministic), and `public_key` is that key's public half. The signing key is never in a vector: each implementation derives it from the 32-byte seed RFC 8032 publishes. Every service refuses this key at boot.

Refusal.description: A refusal vector: verifying `token` with `public_key` at `now` must fail with `reason`. Covers another key (RFC 8032 section 7.1 TEST 2), a tampered payload, algorithm confusion (an HMAC keyed with the public key), a missing signature, another scheme and an over-long lifetime.
